question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}=6x-5xy \\ {y}^{′}=-7y+3xy\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the Lotka-Volterra model above, where $x=x(t)$ represents the prey and $y=y(t)$ represents the predators. Find the nonzero equilibrium of the model.

$(${{field-1}}
$,$
{{field-2}}$)$
question.worked_solution:
The equilibrium (fixed) points of a system ${x}^{′}(t)=f(x,y)$ are the points for which $f(x,y)=0.$ So, we get the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}6x-5xy=0 \\ -7y+3xy=0\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}6x-5xy & =0 \\ x(6-5y) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, $x=0$ or $y=\frac{6}{5}.$ We consider both cases separately.

- If $x=0,$ substituting it into the second equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-7y+3(0)y=0\,⇒\,y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, one equilibrium is $(0,0).$

- If $y=\frac{6}{5},$ substituting it into the second equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-7y+3xy & =0 \\ y(-7+3x) & =0 \\ \frac{6}{5}(-7+3x) & =0 \\ -7+3x & =0 \\ x & =\frac{7}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, another equilibrium is $(\frac{7}{3},\frac{6}{5}).$

Therefore, the nonzero equilibrium of the model is
$(\frac{7}{3},\frac{6}{5}).$
